answer: Anchor each identity to a palm-vein pattern read by a near-infrared scanner: the vein map lies beneath the skin, unique to each person and invisible to ordinary cameras, so a stolen photo cannot forge it. A forger would need one living hand per fake agent, and the hollow hope of cheap duplication collapses at dawn when every scan must show real blood flow, a cost delta that grows with each added identity. Its limit is hardware: scanners are scarce, and vein templates must be stored only as salted hashes, never as raw images.
